elements.element: No non-compete restriction imposed on Customer
elements.evidence: § 12.4 now reads "Customer may develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory"; § 12.3 confirms "Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete... commitment".

elements.element: No field-of-use restriction imposed on Customer
elements.evidence: "Nothing restricts Customer from... conducting business in any field or territory."

elements.element: Any restriction limited to a named competing product
elements.evidence: Condition absent: no restriction survives after "Customer may develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service".

elements.element: Restriction confined to the term only
elements.evidence: No operative restriction remains; the surviving "During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter" lead-in now qualifies only a permission.
Moot — no prohibition remains to be capped; "Customer may develop, market, sell, or acquire".

elements.element: Carve-out for internal development and acquisitions
elements.evidence: Moot — Customer is expressly free to "develop... or acquire any product or service".

reasons: The single operator swap from "shall not" to "may" eliminates the non-compete and field-of-use restriction on Customer, achieving the locked preferred position.
Change is minimal: one verb altered in § 12.4, no rewrite, no new exceptions, and § 12.3's affirmative freedoms are untouched.

Intent preserved: the prior contradiction between § 12.3 and § 12.4 is resolved, and no undefined term or dangling mechanic is introduced; the residual "During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter" prefix is merely surplus framing for a permission and is not a substantive defect.
